findings: The candidate preserves the sparse source boundary and explicitly declares its schema, user-day deduplication and lifecycle-first-login assumptions instead of inventing them as source facts.
Both SQL variants directly answer daily new/old user counts; the NOT EXISTS variant reflects the source hint while the first-date variant exposes the state model clearly.
The answer correctly separates event rows from distinct users so repeated logins on one day do not inflate user counts.
The lifecycle-first-date definition makes new and old mutually exclusive and exhaustive over each day’s distinct active users; independent validation checks that invariant.
Timezone, anonymous-user, history-availability, late-data and large-table access-path boundaries are explicitly called out rather than hidden.
Independent reviewer-owned SQLite execution checks three boundary families and 600 randomized datasets against a separate reference classifier; no semantic mismatch was found.
